paragraphs: Hello! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from Canada with a strong interest in pure mathematics.
My primary interests include algebraic number theory and commutative algebra. This website documents my learning, research projects, expository writing, and mathematical notes.

Outside Mathematics, I am a sprinter and enjoy track and field. I am a 12-time provincial champion in the 100m and 200m. I also have some interest in computer science, though not as much as mathematics :)
Website updates are typically released every 2-4 weeks, though the schedule may vary depending on the time of year.

Hello! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from Canada with a strong passion for pure mathematics. I've been fascinated by numbers, patterns, and mathematical structures since the first grade, and I'm particularly drawn to the beauty and depth of algebraic number theory and commutative algebra.
My goal is to pursue a career in mathematics research and contribute to the field through original work and expository writing.
I'm always happy to connect with fellow mathematics enthusiasts. Please feel free to reach out via the contact page.
Website updates are typically released every 2-4 weeks, though the schedule may vary depending on the time of year.

notes.intro:
Welcome to my collection of mathematical notes. This section is a record of my ongoing study and exploration of mathematics, covering material ranging from olympiad problem solving to undergraduate and graduate-level mathematics. The notes are intended to help me organize what I learn while developing a deeper understanding of the definitions, techniques, proofs, examples, and connections that arise throughout different areas of mathematics.

These notes are different from the more polished and self-contained material in my Expository Writing section. Some may focus on developing the theory of a subject from its foundations, while others may collect results, work through examples and proofs, or explore connections between different areas.

At the moment, this section is still under development, and I do not yet have any notes that I would consider fully complete. New notes will be added and existing ones will be expanded, revised, and refined as my understanding develops. 

The notes are organized into three broad categories: Olympiad Mathematics, Undergraduate Mathematics, and Graduate Mathematics.

expository.subtitle: Mathematical exposition, problem analysis, and experimental mathematics.
paragraphs: Expository writing is one of the most important forms of mathematical communication. Its purpose is not to present new research, but rather to explain existing mathematics in a clear, logical, and accessible way. A well-written exposition bridges the gap between technical rigor and intuition, helping readers understand not only what is true, but also why it is true and how different ideas are connected. This page is my personal collection of expository articles spanning several areas of mathematics. It is organized into sections covering olympiad mathematics, undergraduate topics, and graduate-level subjects, each containing notes, expository essays, problem discussions, and surveys of interesting mathematical ideas. Some articles are intended to introduce foundational concepts, while others provide detailed solutions, commentary, historical context, or connections to more advanced mathematics.
